scope: Focused conditional source boundaries, not cross-owner acceptance

dependencies.meaning: Physical identity helper returns int(First), int(Break) in order; reaction identity similarly converts stored attributes. OA74 uses this provider but never normalizes the internal collection. Decimal normalizer exists but OA72–74 do not invoke it or change prices.

Stopped-A audit producer derives normalized Reaction identity, stores first geometry/confirmation/stop and selected A fields in a new row when absent, then appends unique (source,stop) pairs in encounter order by native equality. OA72 first accepted order follows that list, not a time-sort. Initial records consumer traverses values, normalizes price in its own stage and calls crossing, then sorts by First, confirmation and integer indexes. Accepted rebuild uses initial entry causes/fallback but explicitly skips None source or stop, unlike OA72. OA67 also uses accepted-source membership but with optional None filter; not identical to OA72.

S detector validates direction/range, sorts A by reaction_break_time then int source_index, initializes its physical ledger and invokes stopped-A audit in that A order after clearing ledger. Delegated reaction confirmation and A strict-stop finder govern producer chronology; OA72 does not infer a chronological minimum from it. Sorting source A by reaction-break time does not prove all appended stop times ascending.

Resolve Order context directly imports and calls OA72 once per original input entry via a comprehension, retaining non-None results under original keys. Starts a fresh inherited blocked-First set, adds provisional invalid-leg-head blocks, derives accepted initial First times from retained reaction.first_time (str values parsed by exact format), removes those from blocked set. Distinct conditional E-stop exceptions are derived and optionally emitted, not global unblocking. Returns accepted ledger and blocked times. Native failures can propagate; OA72 does not perform those subsequent lifecycle decisions.

Initial bridge acceptance derives source-time set from S eligible A, calls OA73 on S ledger, passes results as initial_order_audit into E detector. Later source-time set excludes invalid (source_time,int source_index) A pairs, passes to Lifecycle resolve_order_context; resulting accepted_orders/blocked times and distinct E exceptions feed final E detector. Shared reconciliation consumes accepted_orders and E ledger values; presentation A sources separately derived without clipping history. These call sites do not invoke OA74 directly. Time-only projection can collapse distinct source indexes, so OA72 membership does not prove full pair-level validity.

E detector retains truthy initial ledger mapping or substitutes a fresh empty mapping; references of its rows may be shared. Invalid-S root exclusion checks raw behavior physical pair against initial ledger before own B and parent causes; no call to OA74 in these inspected paths. Distinguish initial-order presence from internal identity membership.

limitations: Source-first local review by GPT, not independently staffed. OA72 consumes a caller-defined accepted-source collection; first surviving pair is iteration-order selection, not minimum event time, and source-time membership is not full A identity acceptance. Native container/attribute/equality and malformed input paths remain conditional.

OA72 return can alias the original row or a shallow adjusted row; OA73 retains returned references under original keys. Reiterability is not validated; a one-shot iterable may be consumed. No global proof that all physical key/geometry pairs agree, no new cross-owner acceptance, runtime equality, or production defect asserted.

No RAW payload, runtime, ZIP, production changes, performance measurements, fresh AST generator, or independent SHA-256 claim. Git blob identities and full recursive tree/readback are publication evidence.
